purpose: Collision visibility serialization only; not a semantic, technical or adversarial review verdict.

entries.question: An Azure Container Registry stores several tagged versions of an image named text-normalizer. Which object groups those versions under the image name?
correctAnswerText: Repository
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: A framework team services a compatible base-image release line in ACR. Application build tasks already track that same-registry base image. Security patches must trigger dependent rebuilds without a Dockerfile edit for every patch. Which reference policy fits the build input?
correctAnswerText: Use a stable release-line tag and update it with compatible patches.
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: Two build systems independently number executions and may rebuild the same application commit after different base-image patches. A local build number is unique only within its system. A deployment tag must never be reused and must identify the exact producing execution. Which policy handles both collision sources?
correctAnswerText: Use the system name and its build number as a delimited pair, never reusing the pair.
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: An engineer is studying ACR image representation, rather than selecting a deployment reference. Which two statements describe manifests and layers? Select two.
correctAnswerText: A manifest lists an image’s layers and configuration.
Images can share identical content-addressed layers.
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: A release is serving traffic from a unique ACR image tag. The pipeline needs the documented registry-side write safeguard for that deployed tag, beyond a team convention not to reuse its name. What should it set?
correctAnswerText: The deployed tag’s write-enabled attribute to false
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: An ACR repository has tags latest, 4.2 and 5.0. A developer runs docker pull with the registry and repository name but supplies neither a tag nor a digest. Which tag is requested?
correctAnswerText: latest
entries.subskill: Build, store, version, and manage container images by using Azure Container Registry

entries.question: A developer has source files and a Dockerfile but no local Docker engine. ACR Tasks is already operational and authorized. Which on-demand command builds the source in Azure and pushes the resulting image by default?
correctAnswerText: az acr build
entries.subskill: Build and run images by using Azure Container Registry Tasks

entries.question: An ACR quick build must test a developer’s edited Dockerfile and Python module before either edit is committed. The remote branch and its published tarball still contain the old files. The developer is in the directory containing both edits. Which context should be passed to the build?
correctAnswerText: The local working directory, using .
entries.subskill: Build and run images by using Azure Container Registry Tasks

entries.question: An ACR quick build from a local directory spends most of its time uploading a large folder of training recordings. The Dockerfile does not copy or use that folder. The build output image and application behavior must remain unchanged. Which adjustment targets the measured delay?
correctAnswerText: Exclude the recordings folder with .dockerignore.
entries.subskill: Build and run images by using Azure Container Registry Tasks

entries.question: A conventional Linux App Service app still serves the old build after a new image is pushed to its configured ACR tag. Registry access succeeds; the web app has not restarted and continuous deployment is disabled. The team intentionally keeps this development tag and wants future pushes picked up automatically. Which plan addresses the missing deployment step?
correctAnswerText: Enable container continuous deployment and configure ACR push events to call the returned webhook.
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: A conventional Linux App Service container has sidecar support disabled. Its image pull succeeds and logs show HTTP listening on 0.0.0.0:7000. The current app settings are shown. The deployed image must remain unchanged. Which update corrects the forwarding mismatch?
correctAnswerText: Change WEBSITES_PORT to 7000.
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: A conventional Linux App Service image has an ENTRYPOINT dispatcher that accepts --mode api or --mode batch. Its Dockerfile CMD supplies --mode api, and the dispatcher does not read a mode environment variable. One web app must use batch mode while retaining the image and ENTRYPOINT. Which configuration fits?
correctAnswerText: Set the web app startup command to --mode batch.
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: A Python application in a conventional Linux App Service container reads its Reporting database configuration using the code below. Operations configured Reporting as a SQLAzure connection string, not an ordinary app setting. Which lookup name matches the configured resource?
correctAnswerText: SQLAZURECONNSTR_Reporting
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: An unchanged Linux App Service application reads the secret value from API_KEY in its process environment. A reachable Key Vault must remain the secret’s system of record, without copying its current value into app configuration. The web app identity can read the secret. What should the API_KEY app setting contain?
correctAnswerText: An @Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=...) reference to the secret.
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: A conventional Linux App Service app writes replaceable generated reports to /app/output. Reports must survive app restarts and be visible from every instance after scale-out. The app supports changing its output path; the plan’s shared storage quota is sufficient. Persistent App Service storage is currently disabled. Which plan satisfies both storage requirements?
correctAnswerText: Enable App Service storage and write reports to /home/output.
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: Kudu’s Environment page shows the expected nonsensitive app settings, but its file browser does not show /opt/model inside an App Service image. The engineer needs to inspect that directory and the running application process, not mounted /home files. The authorized engineer’s container image already supports App Service SSH. Which diagnostic surface fits?
correctAnswerText: An SSH session into the running application container
entries.subskill: Deploy containers to Azure App Service, including configuring App Service to supply environment variables and secrets

entries.question: A production Container Apps API calls a worker that must be exposed only inside their shared application environment. Development experiments need a separate environment lifecycle and logging setup. Which placement matches those two boundaries?
correctAnswerText: Place the production services together with internal worker ingress, and development in a different environment.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A Container Apps release plan includes the following configuration changes. Which two create a new revision because they change revision-scoped configuration? Select two.
correctAnswerText: Change the container image reference in properties.template.
Change the scale rules in properties.template.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A Container App uses single revision mode. Its existing revision serves HTTP requests successfully. A replacement revision has provisioned, but it has not passed its configured health checks. Which routing behavior describes this current not-yet-healthy interval, without an operator changing revision mode?
correctAnswerText: Keep serving from the existing revision while the replacement becomes ready.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A Container App has ready revisions v1 and v2 in multiple revision mode. Its application URL sends 90% of HTTP requests to v1 and 10% to v2. Testers need a stable URL dedicated to v2 that can later target a different revision, without changing those weights. Which mechanism fits?
correctAnswerText: Assign an ordinary revision label to v2 and use its label URL.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A single-revision Container App has one authenticated, reachable Service Bus queue scaler. For this observation the queue contains 40 active messages. Using the shown threshold and replica bounds, what desired-count ceiling follows from the backlog calculation, rather than a guarantee of immediately ready replicas?
correctAnswerText: Six replicas
entries.subskill: Implement event-driven scaling by using Kubernetes Event‑driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in Container Apps

entries.question: A single-revision Container Apps worker reads its Service Bus queue successfully using the existing secret bus-connection. Image pulls also succeed. The scaler targets the correct queue but fails authentication; its triggerParameter is connection and its secretRef names a deleted secret. Which change repairs the demonstrated scaler configuration?
correctAnswerText: Map the scaler’s connection parameter to the existing bus-connection secret.
entries.subskill: Implement event-driven scaling by using Kubernetes Event‑driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in Container Apps

entries.question: A Container Apps pipeline applies containerapp.yml and also supplies --image with the new release tag. The applied template still contains the old image, which remains in the YAML. The team requires the version-controlled YAML to remain the configuration source of truth. Which repair matches the documented CLI behavior?
correctAnswerText: Edit the image value inside the YAML and apply that file.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A Container Apps template sets API_KEY using the JSON fragment below. Secret provider-key holds the required production credential; backup-key holds a different test-provider credential. Both exist. The unchanged production application receives the literal string secretref:provider-key. Secret values must stay outside the template. Which entry supplies the intended credential?
correctAnswerText: {"name":"API_KEY","secretRef":"provider-key"}
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: A Container App has a system-assigned identity with the required ACR pull permission, and the registry network path works. Its registry entry still selects username/password authentication. The team wants future revision pulls to use the assigned identity without stored registry credentials. Which configuration change selects that identity for image pulls?
correctAnswerText: Update the ACR registry entry with --identity system.
entries.subskill: Deploy applications to Azure Container Apps, including environment configuration and revision management

entries.question: Two new Container Apps revisions fail in different stages. Revision A never starts its application because the image cannot be pulled. Revision B pulls and starts but the application throws an exception when processing a test request. An operator has log access. Which initial evidence pairing targets the two failure layers?
correctAnswerText: A: system logs; B: application console logs.
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: A single-revision Container Apps worker consumes the enrich subscription of the Service Bus topic documents. Another application consumes audit from the same topic. Authentication is already configured. The enrich worker must scale from its own active-message backlog, not the other subscriber’s backlog. Which event-source metadata identifies that work?
correctAnswerText: topicName=documents and subscriptionName=enrich on the Service Bus scaler
entries.subskill: Implement event-driven scaling by using Kubernetes Event‑driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in Container Apps

entries.question: A Container App combines a cron scale rule and an HTTP scale rule with minReplicas=2 and maxReplicas=9. During the active cron window, cron requests 7 replicas and the HTTP metric requests 11. Later, outside that window, the HTTP metric requests 3. Ignore transition timing and consider only the desired count after rule combination and bounds. Which pair follows?
correctAnswerText: During: 9; later: 3
entries.subskill: Implement event-driven scaling by using Kubernetes Event‑driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in Container Apps

entries.question: A single-revision Container Apps worker uses an Event Hubs scaler and one consumer group over four partitions. Four replicas are already processing all four partitions, one assigned consumer per partition, but lag grows. The partition count and consumer group must remain unchanged. Which conclusion about scaling follows from this topology?
correctAnswerText: Raising maxReplicas alone cannot add more simultaneous partition readers to this consumer group.
entries.subskill: Implement event-driven scaling by using Kubernetes Event‑driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in Container Apps

entries.question: A new Container Apps revision normally needs 90 seconds to load its model. Logs show steady progress, but an early liveness failure repeatedly restarts it. Its readiness endpoint currently returns success as soon as the web server starts, before inference is usable. Which two changes address the separate restart and premature-routing problems? Select two.
correctAnswerText: Adjust liveness initial delay to accommodate measured normal model initialization.
Change readiness to report success only when inference can be served.
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: An AKS release must change a Deployment from image v1 with two replicas to image v2 with three replicas. The image is accessible, configuration is compatible and cluster capacity is sufficient. The desired release must be reproducible from source control and survive individual Pod replacement. Which update records the requested state?
correctAnswerText: Set the Deployment template image to v2 and spec.replicas to 3, apply the manifest, then verify readiness.
entries.subskill: Deploy and manage applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) by using manifest files

entries.question: An AKS namespace contains ConfigMap app-settings with key LOG_LEVEL and Secret api-credentials with key TOKEN. A Deployment in that namespace must inject these existing values as environment variables without copying their contents into the manifest. Which two references match? Select two.
correctAnswerText: LOG_LEVEL: valueFrom.configMapKeyRef with name app-settings and key LOG_LEVEL
TOKEN: valueFrom.secretKeyRef with name api-credentials and key TOKEN
entries.subskill: Deploy and manage applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) by using manifest files

entries.question: This AKS Service selects healthy Pods that listen on TCP port 8080. In-cluster clients must continue using Service port 8443. Which field change repairs the forwarding mismatch while preserving the client-facing contract?
correctAnswerText: Change targetPort from 9000 to 8080.
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: A single-container AKS Pod named text-api-pod in namespace ai-workloads is in CrashLoopBackOff. Events show successful scheduling and image pulls. The previous container instance terminated during initialization, while the current one has produced little output. Which command targets the terminated instance’s application output?
correctAnswerText: kubectl logs text-api-pod -n ai-workloads --previous
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: An AKS Service selects app=text-service. Its intended Ready Pods have app=text-api, and no Pod has the selected label. The Service resolves in DNS but its EndpointSlices have no backing Pod addresses. Ports are correct, and the Deployment labels must remain unchanged. Which focused repair and validation fit?
correctAnswerText: Set the Service selector to app=text-api, inspect EndpointSlices and send a request through the Service.
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: Each of two AKS nodes has 3 GiB available for additional Pod memory requests. A new Deployment requests 4 GiB per Pod, limits memory to 6 GiB and needs two replicas. Both Pods remain Pending with Insufficient memory events. Tests require at least a 4 GiB request, and all other scheduling conditions are satisfied. Which plan addresses placement without under-requesting the workload?
correctAnswerText: Provide nodes with at least 4 GiB of available request capacity for each needed Pod.
entries.subskill: Deploy and manage applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) by using manifest files

entries.question: Three AKS Deployments consume one mutable ConfigMap that has just been updated. A reads its value from an environment variable at process startup. B reads a file mounted with subPath. C uses an ordinary ConfigMap volume and rereads the file per request; its file already shows the new value. Which focused rollout plan updates the remaining consumers without restarting C?
correctAnswerText: Restart A and B; leave C running.
entries.subskill: Deploy and manage applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) by using manifest files

entries.question: An authorized AKS operator must confirm that Secret api-credentials contains the key TOKEN without displaying its value. Which command shows the Secret’s metadata and key information for this check?
correctAnswerText: kubectl describe secret api-credentials
entries.subskill: Deploy and manage applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) by using manifest files

entries.question: During an AKS rollout, an engineer receives HTTP 200 through a local kubectl port-forward to the API Service. The release gate requires clients to reach the expected inference route through the configured public ingress hostname. Public access still fails. Which next check tests the requirement that the local tunnel did not cover?
correctAnswerText: Inspect the ingress address and host/path backend mapping, then request the expected public route from an external client.
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity

entries.question: AKS namespaces production and staging each contain a Pod named worker-0, and each Pod has containers api and proxy. The current kubectl context defaults to staging. The operator needs the production application’s current logs, not the proxy logs. Which explicit command selects both required boundaries?
correctAnswerText: kubectl logs worker-0 -c api -n production
entries.subskill: Monitor and troubleshoot solutions on AKS and Container Apps by inspecting logs, events, and end-to-end connectivity
